original_question: Let μ be a non-negative finite Borel measure on R^3 representing an extended nuclear charge distribution, with total charge μ(R^3) ≤ 1. Consider the Dirac-Coulomb operator D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}, where D0 is the free Dirac operator and μ * |x|^{-1} is the electrostatic potential generated by μ. Denote by λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) the lowest eigenvalue of this operator in the spectral gap (-1, 1). Is this eigenvalue always minimized, among all such charge distributions with the same total charge, when the entire charge is concentrated at one point, so that λ1(D0 - μ * |x|^{-1}) ≥ λ1(D0 - μ(R^3)/|x|) = sqrt(1 - μ(R^3)^2)?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1: for each fixed total charge ν in [0,1], the first gap eigenvalue of the Dirac operator D0−μ*|x|^{-1} should be minimized by the point charge νδ0, so that λ1(D0−μ*|x|^{-1}) ≥ λ1(D0−ν/|x|)=√(1−ν^2). The chapter abstract and the opening of Section 34.1 identify exactly this as the main question. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-12244-6_34))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s central object and comparison almost exactly: a non-negative finite Borel measure μ on R^3, the electrostatic potential μ*|x|^{-1}, the Dirac operator D0, the first eigenvalue in the spectral gap, the fixed-total-charge comparison, and the special role of the fully concentrated point charge. This is precisely how the chapter frames the open problem. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-12244-6_34))
missing_details: State the ambient Hilbert space: the operator acts on L^2(R^3,C^4).
Define the free Dirac operator explicitly as D0 = -i α·∇ + β, in the units m = c = ħ = 1 used in the paper.
Introduce the fixed mass parameter ν := μ(R^3) and quantify the problem for every fixed ν in [0,1], rather than only saying “among all such charge distributions with the same total charge.”

Use the paper-faithful operator language: strictly speaking one should refer to the distinguished self-adjoint realization (or first min-max level in the gap) of D0−μ*|x|^{-1}, not just a formal differential expression.
Mention the point charge as νδ0 (or νδx0), with the origin chosen without loss of generality by translation invariance.
Clarify that the comparison value λ1(D0−ν/|x|)=√(1−ν^2) is the hydrogenic one-centre value used as the benchmark in the conjecture.

If one wants complete faithfulness at the critical endpoint, note the paper’s care with the distinguished extension / min-max formulation, which is more precise than the bare phrase “lowest eigenvalue.”
refined_question: For a fixed ν in [0,1], let μ be a non-negative finite Borel measure on R^3 with μ(R^3)=ν, let Vμ(x)=∫R^3 |x−y|^(-1) dμ(y), and let Hμ be the distinguished self-adjoint realization on L^2(R^3,C^4) of Hμ = D0−Vμ, where D0 = −i α·∇ + β in units m=c=ħ=1. Is the first gap eigenvalue (equivalently, the first min-max level in the paper’s setup) always bounded below by the one-centre hydrogenic value, namely λ1(Hμ) ≥ λ1(D0−ν/|x|)=√(1−ν^2), so that among all non-negative charge distributions of total charge ν the most attractive one is the point charge νδ0 (up to translation)?
justification: I did not broaden your draft beyond the chapter’s main conjectural question. The chapter abstract says the main question is whether the lowest eigenvalue is minimal when the nuclear charge is concentrated at one single point, and the opening of Section 34.1 develops exactly the nonrelativistic analogue before passing to the Dirac setting. Your draft is therefore targeting the main fixed-mass point-concentration conjecture, not a neighboring optimizer-existence or critical-mass statement. The main sharpening needed is to adopt the paper’s precise spectral language—distinguished self-adjoint realization / first min-max level in the gap—and to quantify at fixed ν := μ(R^3). ([researchportal.ip-paris.fr](https://researchportal.ip-paris.fr/en/publications/which-nuclear-shape-generates-the-strongest-attraction-on-a-relat/))
